versions.short: The bill would require the Department of Homeland Security's Office of Intelligence and Analysis to set up standardized basic training for all of its employees, with new hires starting within 90 days of their official start date and before beginning their duties. It would also add extra training for analysts on the office's mission, intelligence analysis standards, and writing and sourcing rules, and for open source intelligence collectors on collection methods, data handling, and legal limits. The office would be required to offer specialized and advanced courses, publish a list of outside training each quarter, and track employee completion of training. The training requirements would take effect one year after enactment, and the Under Secretary would report to Congress on the program, with the Comptroller General later comparing the curriculum to other intelligence and Defense Department training.
